claims.claim: IonQ's structural thesis links semiconductor-style trapped-ion fabrication to repeatable quantum-system manufacturing, then to deployable systems and eventual useful fault-tolerant compute; the current evidence validates early manufacturing and commercial milestones, not the full chain.

Successor bottlenecks are performance/reliability, fabrication yield, error correction, system integration and economic utility; any can break the path from prototype manufacturing to durable human/enterprise value.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Vertical fabrication can reduce a manufacturability bottleneck, but fault tolerance and economic utility remain unresolved bottlenecks.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Platform breadth and manufacturing integration provide optionality, while useful quantum advantage remains technology- and workload-dependent.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Competing quantum modalities and classical/accelerated computing remain credible substitutes until workload-level advantage is established.

risks.risk: Manufacturing scale can improve while fault-tolerant performance or economic utility still fails to materialize.

causalEdges.mechanism: fabrication integration can shorten iteration cycles and increase manufacturing throughput
causalEdges.falsifier: yield, reliability or performance fails to scale

causalEdges.mechanism: manufacturable systems can support more customer installations
causalEdges.falsifier: deliveries or RPO conversion stall despite production milestones

causalEdges.mechanism: customers retain and expand use only if systems solve valuable workloads competitively
causalEdges.falsifier: classical or rival quantum approaches remain superior on target workloads

unknowns.unknown: Independent Superion 256 performance validation and production yields are not established in reviewed evidence.
Fault-tolerant workload economics remain unproven by the reviewed milestones.

claims.claim: Rapid revenue and RPO growth are genuine commercial signals, but they do not establish organic growth quality, fault-tolerant technical success or long-run unit economics; acquisition effects are an explicit confounder.
Prototype fabrication and first trapped ions are milestones, not independent proof of production yield, reliability or useful fault-tolerant advantage.

factors.name: thesisQuality
factors.basis: Commercial and manufacturing milestones strengthen the thesis while the hardest technical/economic gates remain unproven.

factors.name: financialOperatingMomentum
factors.basis: Revenue/RPO growth is strong but acquisition contribution complicates interpretation of organic execution.

risks.risk: Acquisition-driven growth can inflate headline growth without equivalent organic platform traction.
Competing modalities and classical accelerators can delay or reduce the addressable workloads that produce economic quantum advantage.
Roadmap and product-launch language can create confidence inflation if prototype milestones are treated as equivalent to fault-tolerant commercial performance.

causalEdges.from: technical roadmap slippage or weak independent validation
causalEdges.mechanism: customers may defer deployments if promised performance/yield is not demonstrated
causalEdges.falsifier: independent performance and delivery evidence validates roadmap on schedule

contradictions.claimA: Revenue and RPO are growing rapidly.
contradictions.claimB: Commercialization remains early relative to the fault-tolerant roadmap and growth includes acquisition effects.
contradictions.disposition: growth is real but quality/organic attribution and long-run economics remain unresolved; not a present blocker.

unknowns.unknown: Independent benchmark validation, production yield and useful fault-tolerant economics remain unestablished.
No source-addressed current dilution/governance assessment is established in reviewed Beta inputs.
